newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG Metals says copper shipment "commercial trade".
newsitem.headline: LG Metals says copper shipment "commercial trade".

text.p: South Korea's LG Metals Corp said on Thursday it had sold about 10,000 tonnes of copper supplied by Chile's Codelco to European metal firm Metallgesellschaft and the cargo would be shipped to Singapore.
"It is just commercial trade," spokesman Lee In-soo told Reuters by telephone, adding the cargo had been sold to MG.
Asked whether the cargo would go to the London Metal Exchange's (LME) warehouse in Singapore, Lee said he had no further information.

Earlier on Thursday, Asian metal traders said a cargo of 10,000 tonnes of copper was reported to be sitting in South Korea's southeastern port of Pusan awaiting shipment to Singapore at the end of June or early July.
"The arrival in Singapore is set for the second week of July," one trade source said.

Some traders in Seoul said earlier that the current slump in South Korean base metals demand, caused by an economic slowdown after a series of corporate collapses, had forced LG Metals to ship its copper stocks overseas.
Other traders said the shipment could be aimed at covering LG Metals' short copper positions on the LME or was just a commercial trade.

Earlier this month the LG Metals spokesman said the metals market had "no need to worry" about its current open LME metal options positions, but declined to comment on rumours in London the firm was facing huge losses after a copper rally in early June.
